Identity & Architecture

After Sixteen Years, Fiatjaf Concedes: Petnames Are Actually Good

The protocol’s creator reverses a long-held position against local human-readable handles, pointing toward path-based resolution while firmly rejecting calls for centralized AI discovery.

Protocol Desk · Dispatches from fiatjaf, Ben Arc, and david

For sixteen years, the prevailing doctrine in decentralized public-key networks held that global hexadecimal identities and external DNS-tethered NIP-05 identifiers were sufficient to anchor persona without the semantic complexity of local namespaces. That posture shifted abruptly on Friday when fiatjaf, the creator of Nostr, announced an unambiguous reversal: After 16 years I've decided that petnames are actually good. The brief concession prompted an immediate reaction from hardware developer Ben Arc, who observed that he had never encountered the concept prior to meeting fiatjaf and had assumed it was already favored.

In subsequent discussion, fiatjaf elaborated on how petname chains could resolve human-readable identities across contact graphs without creating a central registry or squatting incentives: "fiatjaf.com" is NIP-05, "triangles_nbot" is a petname in my contact list. Under this schema, a signed-in client could locate third-party pubkeys via relative paths such as ~/fiatjaf/triangles_nbot, leaning on established webs of trust rather than global claims.

The naming debate dovetailed into a contentious exchange over discovery and algorithmic feeds. A participant writing under the handle someone argued that Nostr’s persistent barrier is finding niche interest communities when Bitcoin discussions dominate public feeds, proposing that thin clients cannot handle discovery and suggesting that relay operators or server-side machine learning should construct tailored echo chambers for users pro bono.

Fiatjaf offered a sharp refusal: Luckily for me I don't think humanity needs a centralized AI-powered global "discovery" layer, so I don't have to try to build that. He suggested that users demanding global algorithmic routing are seeking architecture closer to the AT Protocol than Nostr’s relay model. Meanwhile, developer david clarified that keyword search on unranked indexes already isolates subjects without popularity contests, adding that verified community tagging for long-form articles is currently being rolled out across clients.

Central Banking & Sovereignty

One Call to Athens: Lagarde Blocks Binance at the Aegean Border

ECB president reportedly bypassed formal regulatory review to halt MiCA licensing in Greece, fearful that dollar stablecoins would overtake Frankfurt’s digital euro.

Monetary Affairs · Reports surfaced by LL62 and Copinmalin

Reports circulating across European feeds detailed an extraordinary executive intervention into cryptocurrency licensing. According to Wall Street Journal reporting surfaced by analyst LL62, ECB President Christine Lagarde personally intervened to block Binance's MiCA license application in Greece, first reported by The Wall Street Journal on September 18, 2026.

Discussions surrounding the incident revealed that Lagarde allegedly called Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis directly to ask him not to approve the application, per WSJ sources familiar with the discussions. The motivation cited behind the pressure was institutional defensiveness: fear that Binance's scale as the world's largest exchange would deepen dollar-stablecoin adoption across the EU, threatening the European Central Bank's digital euro project.

The revelation provoked disbelief across French and European trading circles. Copinmalin asked: C'est incroyable cette histoire ! Comment va réagir binance ? LL62 underscored the governance precedent: Millions of EU users woke up unable to trade because one bureaucrat made a phone call. No court order, no formal rejection, no documented legal channel.

Decentralized Systems

Pillars of Propagation: Surviving the Broken Wire

Long-Form Desk · Arjen’s essay highlighted by Gigi

In an essay titled Pillars of Propagation, author Arjen posed a fundamental question about network topology: What if we can live in a way where we wouldn't even notice that the internet is down. (Gigi) Marked passages detailed how self-authenticating events transform routing: After receiving data from a far-away relay, that same connection is NEVER AGAIN needed for the same information to propagate. (Citation)

Under this distribution model, localized nodes replicate data organically without persistent reliance on transit backbones: Now that this data exists in my local community, ANYONE in need of this information can retrieve it from me rather than the far-away place. (Citation) Because signatures allow verifying authenticity independently of transport: Because the data integrity can be validated from the data itself, the data can flow freely. (Citation)

Zeus LN Issues Candidate v13.2.2 with iOS Multi-Device Advisory

The developers of the Zeus mobile lightning node published a new testing build: ZEUS v13.2.2-rc1 is now available for testing. Alongside the release, the team issued an advisory for Apple users running the wallet concurrently on more than one device, urging them to review keychain handling instructions before upgrading.

Across the Zapstore app index, seventeen software updates were published today, including Bisq Easy for peer-to-peer fiat-bitcoin exchange on Android, Flexify for offline workout logging, and Colota for private self-hosted GPS tracking.

Dark Wire · Statecraft

BlackCore Exposed: Commercial Disinformation in the Feed

Citizen Lab documentation shows commercial firms training government operators to generate artificial consensus on social platforms.

TFTC highlighted findings exposing BlackCore, an influence-for-hire firm training state personnel: Governments are running influence operations on social media right now. Not hypothetically. Documented.

LL62 noted how accessible synthetic perception management has become: The ability to put propaganda in front of you, make it look like ordinary people talking, and get you emotionally invested in an argument has become incredibly accessible.

The operational defense remains epistemological vigilance: Fall back to first principles. What do you know? What are you assuming? Who benefits from you being angry at this particular thing, at this particular moment? (Citation)
